# Distribution when the platforms are closed

Source: https://lowob.com/research/distribution-when-the-platforms-are-closed/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-03-17 · Updated: 2026-11-16
Function: Distribution

> Summary: Rank channels by the cost of earning a buyer's attention and start where trust is borrowed: partners, referrals, creators and owned media. Sort every channel into open, restricted or closed for your category first, using the platforms' own dated policies. Paid media comes last, once you know what converts.

Rank channels by the cost of earning a buyer's attention, and start where the attention is cheapest and the trust is borrowed: partners, referrals, creators and owned media. Paid media comes last, once you know what converts. Before any of that, sort every channel into open, restricted or closed for your category and geography, using the platforms' own published policies with the date you checked them.

## Three bands, before any plan

Before planning distribution, sort every channel into one of three bands for your category and geography.

**Open:** you can use it without pre-approval. Partners, affiliates, creators, email, content, events, much of programmatic.

**Restricted:** usable with documentation, licensing or approval. Plan for it only once the paperwork clears; never put it in a forecast before then.

**Closed:** will not carry you in this market today. Name it early and plan without it.

The bands are real and published. Google's cryptocurrency policy lets exchanges and software wallets advertise in approved markets once certified, which is restricted. It bans ads for initial coin offerings, DeFi trading protocols, token liquidity pools and crypto loans regardless of location, which is closed. TikTok's financial services policy lists crypto as not allowed in some markets and as permitted with licensing and 18+ targeting in others. The same product can sit in three bands across three countries.

Web3 teams often discover their closed band after a campaign is built. AI teams rarely face closed bands, but face crowded ones where costs climb fast. Either way, the sort comes first. Our explainer on [what a restricted category is](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-restricted-category/) sets out how platforms make the assignment.

## The channel ladder

| Order | Channel | Why it works early | Watch out for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Partners and integrations | Borrowed trust; your customer is already there | Partnerships with no named owner or shared goal |
| 2 | Affiliates and referrals | Paid on results; scales with proof | Disclosure rules; quality of referred users |
| 3 | Creators and KOLs | Trusted voice to a specific audience | Paying for reach not fit; disclosure; one-off posts |
| 4 | Owned media | Compounds; you keep the audience and the data | Slow to start; needs a point of view |
| 5 | Answer engines | Buyers increasingly ask AI assistants who to use | Thin or inconsistent public information about you |
| 6 | Paid media | Scale, once conversion is known | Spending before you know what converts |

The order is a ranking by the cost of earning attention, not by size. Paid can be the largest channel eventually. It is last because it is the most expensive place to learn what converts.

## Partners first

The best early partner is someone who has your customer and gains something when you succeed. For a DeFi protocol, every asset issuer whose token you support has a reason to promote a new use for it. For an AI tool, the platform you integrate with often runs a marketplace, a partner directory or co-marketing for apps that make it stickier.

The weight of evidence in technology markets points the same way. Canalys, an analyst firm, forecast that 70% of customer spending on technology, IT services and telecom services would go through partners in 2025. Forrester's 2025 buyers' journey survey, cited in a February 2026 post, found an average of nine people from outside the buying organisation involved in a purchase decision. Much of a buyer's trust is formed by people who are not you. [What is ecosystem-led growth?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-ecosystem-led-growth/) covers how firms use partner overlap to reach those buyers.

Write the shared goal down before the first call: what each side gets, what each side does, and the single first use case you will launch together. A partnership without a first use case is a logo swap. [Partner channel design](https://lowob.com/research/partner-channel-design/) covers roles and payment by partner type, and [co-selling with platforms](https://lowob.com/research/co-selling-with-platforms/) covers the case where the partner is a cloud or software platform.

> A partnership without a first use case is a logo swap.

## Affiliates and creators, done properly

Affiliates and referral partners are paid on results, which makes them the natural second rung: the company pays when something it can verify has happened. The terms decide whether the programme builds an asset or leaks margin to coupon sites. Our piece on [building an affiliate programme without paying for coupon leaks](https://lowob.com/research/affiliate-program-asset-or-coupon-leak/) covers the terms.

Pay creators for a job, not a post: a tutorial, a walkthrough, an honest review, a live session. Match on audience fit, not follower count. Require clear disclosure every time, both because the rules require it and because undisclosed promotion is exactly what erodes trust in crypto and AI alike.

The disclosure rule is specific. The US Federal Trade Commission's guidance says a disclosure belongs with the endorsement, not on a profile page or behind a "more" link; in video it goes in the video; on a livestream it is repeated. Plain words such as "ad" or "sponsored" work; "sp" and "collab" do not, and a platform's built-in tool may not be enough. Financial and crypto promotions carry further rules in most markets, which belong in the creator brief.

| Creator brief field | What it contains |
| --- | --- |
| The job | Tutorial, walkthrough, review or live session, with the outcome it should produce |
| Audience fit | Who watches, and why they match the customer you chose |
| Approved claims | The claims the creator may make, and the ones they may not |
| Disclosure | The exact words and where they appear |
| Payment | Per verified outcome where possible, not per post |

## Owned media and answer engines

These two are linked. When a buyer asks an AI assistant "what is the best tool for X?", the answer is assembled from what is published about you and your category. Clear, specific, consistent public material, such as docs, comparisons, research and case studies, is now distribution, not just marketing.

The shift is measurable. Pew Research Center tracked 900 US adults' Google searches in March 2025 and found users clicked a traditional result on 8% of visits when an AI summary appeared, against 15% when one did not. If fewer buyers click through, the summary is often the first impression, and it is built from whatever sources the engine trusts. Our pieces on [how LLMs choose sources](https://lowob.com/research/how-llms-choose-sources/) and [owned channels](https://lowob.com/research/owned-channels-email-content/) cover the mechanics.

Check what the major assistants say about you today. If it is wrong or missing, that is a content gap, and it is cheaper to fix than any paid channel.

## Paid comes last, and how to know when

Paid media becomes the right next channel when three things are true. The company knows which offer converts, from the open-band channels. It knows its cost per verified outcome in those channels, so a paid result has a benchmark. And any restricted-band approval has actually cleared. Until then, paid spend buys expensive lessons the cheaper channels would have taught.

## The checklist

| Item | Done when |
| --- | --- |
| Band map | Every channel sorted into open, restricted or closed, per market, with the policy page and date checked |
| Partners | Three named partners with a first use case each |
| Referral or affiliate offer | Terms set, with clear disclosure |
| Creator brief | Pays for a job, not a post |
| Answer engines | What AI assistants say about you, checked and logged |
| Paid | Budget held until conversion is known |

## lowob takeaways

- **Sort before you plan.** Open, restricted or closed, per market, from the platforms' own dated policies.
- **Start where the customer already is.** Partners and integrations borrow trust you have not yet earned.
- **Pay creators for a job and disclose every time.** Placement of the disclosure matters as much as its presence.
- **Treat answer engines as a channel.** Fewer clicks reach the page; the summary is the first impression.
- **Hold paid until conversion is known.** It is the most expensive place to learn.
